one: Machine learning theory: generalization bounds, non-convex optimization, and implicit regularization — why deep learning works.
pos: CS 229M (STATS 214) is the most mathematically demanding ML course, aimed at graduate students who want to do theory. It does not teach model tuning; it trains you to analyze modern large-scale nonlinear models with concentration inequalities, uniform convergence, and optimization theory.
topics: **Generalization theory**: uniform convergence, VC dimension, Rademacher complexity
**Non-convex optimization**: gradient descent, saddle points, landscape
**Implicit regularization**: overparameterization, double descent, margin stability
**Unsupervised learning and domain adaptation**: representation learning theory
**Modern model analysis**: approximation and generalization of Transformers/deep networks
assess: Assignments plus a final/project, mostly proofs and paper reading. Check the current syllabus for details.
who: People who want to do ML theory, a PhD, or rigorous analysis; also suitable for math/statistics backgrounds moving into ML.
tips: Brush up on real analysis and probability first. Don't expect to understand it in one pass — work through the notes and papers repeatedly.
note: Not offered in the 2026–27 ExploreCourses listing.
